facts.statement: The type species Dianchungosaurus lufengensis was described in 1982.
facts.quote: The type species is D. lufengensis and it was described in 1982.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dianchungosaurus were found in the Lower Lufeng Formation near Dianchung in Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: Both remains come from the Lower Lufeng Formation, near Dianchung, in the Yunnan Province in China.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Sinemurian stage of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: The age of the material is thus Sinemurian (Early Jurassic).

facts.statement: Dianchungosaurus was originally thought to be a dinosaur but was reclassified as a mesoeucrocodylian by Paul Barrett and Xing Xu in 2005.
facts.quote: It was previously considered a dinosaur, but it was recently reclassified as a mesoeucrocodylian by Paul Barrett and Xing Xu (2005).

facts.statement: A 2005 study by Barrett and Xu determined that the specimens originally assigned to Dianchungosaurus formed a chimera of different animals.
facts.quote: In 2005, a paper by Barrett and Xu focused on this problematic taxon and found its specimens to form an hypodigm, a chimera of different animals.

facts.statement: The name Dianchungosaurus lufengensis is retained for the holotype to maintain stability in the literature, while the paratype awaits formal description.
facts.quote: To maintain the stability in the literature, the holotype retains the name D. lufengensis, while the paratype awaits a formal description.

facts.statement: Dianchungosaurus lived between 199.5 and 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Sinemurian (199.5 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Dianchungosaurus means "Dianchung lizard" and is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian crocodyliform from the Early Jurassic of China.
rejected.quote: Dianchungosaurus (meaning "Dianchung lizard") is an extinct genus of mesoeucrocodylian crocodyliform from the Early Jurassic of China.
